# 1960s Music

Tune in to 1960s music: eight genre stations from British Invasion to Motown, hundreds of essential songs, and free interactive tools you can play now.

Sitemap: https://1960smusic.net/sitemap.xml

## Tools
- [Random Song Generator](https://1960smusic.net/tools/random-song/): Hit generate and let the decade pick a track for you, from any of the eight genres, playing right on the page.
- [Party Playlist Builder](https://1960smusic.net/tools/playlist-builder/): Pick a vibe such as upbeat, romantic or dance, and build a shuffled playlist to match the mood.
- [Music Trivia](https://1960smusic.net/tools/trivia/): A ten-question round drawn from real facts about the decade's greatest records. Keep score, then play again.
- [What's Your 60s Sound?](https://1960smusic.net/tools/quiz/): Answer seven quick questions and discover which 1960s genre is your personal soundtrack.
- [Radio Dial](https://1960smusic.net/tools/radio/): A continuous, station-style listening experience that rotates through each genre.
- [Daily Guessing Game](https://1960smusic.net/tools/daily/): Watch a 1960s music video and guess its release year. Fifteen elimination-style levels, one wrong guess ends the run.
- [60s Music Crossword](https://1960smusic.net/tools/60s-music-crossword/): A 55-clue crossword pulling songs, artists and genre terms from every station on the dial.

## Year Guides
- [1960s Music by Year: 1960-1969 Year Guides](https://1960smusic.net/1960s/): 1960s music broken down year by year: number one hits, key albums and genre shifts for 1960 through 1969, each with a playable tracklist.
- [1960 Music: The Year's Biggest Hit Songs and Albums](https://1960smusic.net/1960s/1960/): 1960 music delivered 19 different Billboard number ones, Elvis Presley's record year, and the first steps toward Nashville, Brill Building and surf sounds.
- [1961 Music: The Year's Biggest Hit Songs and Albums](https://1960smusic.net/1960s/1961/): 1961 music brought Motown its first number one, Patsy Cline's Nashville Sound breakthrough, and 22 different Billboard chart toppers across the year.
- [1962 Music: The Year's Biggest Hit Songs and Albums](https://1960smusic.net/1960s/1962/): 1962 music brought The Twist back to No. 1, Ray Charles crossed into Nashville, and the Four Seasons topped the chart with their first two singles.
- [1963 Music: The Year's Biggest Hit Songs and Albums](https://1960smusic.net/1960s/1963/): 1963 music crowned Surfin' U.S.A. the year's top song even though it only reached No. 3, while Beatlemania swept Britain months before the US Hot 100 noticed.
- [1964 Music: The Year's Biggest Hit Songs and Albums](https://1960smusic.net/1960s/1964/): 1964 music belonged to the Beatles, who held all five top Hot 100 spots on April 4 and took six number ones, 18 weeks in all.
- [1965 Music: The Year's Biggest Hit Songs and Albums](https://1960smusic.net/1960s/1965/): 1965 music crowned Wooly Bully, a song that never reached number one, while the Beatles took five number ones and 12 weeks at the top.
- [1966 Music: The Year's Biggest Hit Songs and Albums](https://1960smusic.net/1960s/1966/): 1966 music crowned The Ballad of the Green Berets, a five-week number one, while 27 different songs topped the Billboard Hot 100.
- [1967 Music: The Year's Biggest Hit Songs and Albums](https://1960smusic.net/1960s/1967/): 1967 music crowned Lulu's To Sir With Love, a five-week number one, while 19 different songs topped the Billboard Hot 100.
- [1968 Music: The Year's Biggest Hit Songs and Albums](https://1960smusic.net/1960s/1968/): 1968 music crowned the Beatles' Hey Jude, a nine-week number one, while 16 different songs topped the Billboard Hot 100.
- [1969 Music: The Year's Biggest Hit Songs and Albums](https://1960smusic.net/1960s/1969/): 1969 music crowned the Archies' Sugar, Sugar, a four-week number one, while 17 different songs topped the Billboard Hot 100.

## About the Author
- [About Charlie](https://1960smusic.net/about/charlie/): Meet Charlie, the retired Alberta music lover who researches, writes and fact-checks every page on 1960smusic.net, from song stories to On This Day.

## Genre Hubs
- [60s Rock: How the Decade Went from Garage Bands to Psychedelia](https://1960smusic.net/blog/genres/60s-rock/): 60s rock explained: how British Invasion, garage, folk rock, and psychedelic bands turned a three-chord sound into the decade's biggest music, year by year.
- [Garage Rock: The Raw, Fuzzed-Out Sound of 1960s America](https://1960smusic.net/blog/genres/garage-surf-rock/): Garage rock explained: how fuzz guitars, cheap organs, and teenage garages built the raw sound of 1960s America, from Louie Louie to the Nuggets revival.
- [1960s Country Music: Nashville Sound vs. Bakersfield Sound](https://1960smusic.net/blog/genres/country-60s/): 1960s country music split into two rival camps: Nashville's polished strings and Bakersfield's twangy honky-tonk. Meet the sounds, artists, and hits.
- [Brill Building Pop: The 1960s Hit Factory Explained](https://1960smusic.net/blog/genres/pop-brill-building/): Brill Building Pop ruled early 1960s radio from one crowded Manhattan office, pairing songwriting teams like Goffin-King with girl groups and teen idols.
- [1960s Easy Listening Music: The Complete Genre Guide](https://1960smusic.net/blog/genres/jazz-easy-listening/): 1960s easy listening music paired crooners and orchestras with the bossa nova craze and Oscar-winning film themes, from Sinatra to Astrud Gilberto.
- [Motown Music: How Detroit's Hit Factory Ruled the Charts](https://1960smusic.net/blog/genres/motown-soul/): How Berry Gordy's Detroit hit factory and its Southern soul rivals built the sound that crossed over America's pop charts.
- [Folk Rock: How Bob Dylan and The Byrds Changed 1960s Music](https://1960smusic.net/blog/genres/folk-rock/): How Bob Dylan going electric and The Byrds' jangly cover of Mr. Tambourine Man built one of the decade's most literate, most political sounds.
- [Psychedelic Rock: How LSD and Feedback Changed 1960s Music](https://1960smusic.net/blog/genres/psychedelic-rock/): How San Francisco acid rock and British studio experimentation reshaped 1960s music between 1965 and 1969.
- [British Invasion: How 1960s British Rock Bands Conquered America](https://1960smusic.net/blog/genres/british-invasion/): How UK bands led by The Beatles conquered American radio, charts, and TV starting in 1964, and the sound and artists that defined the movement.

## Artists
- [Jefferson Airplane: Band History, Members and Hits](https://1960smusic.net/blog/artists/jefferson-airplane/): Jefferson Airplane formed in San Francisco in 1965, added Grace Slick in 1966 and hit the Top 10 with Somebody to Love and White Rabbit in 1967.
- [Herb Alpert & The Tijuana Brass: Whipped Cream and No. 1s](https://1960smusic.net/blog/artists/herb-alpert-and-the-tijuana-brass/): Herb Alpert & The Tijuana Brass turned a 1962 trumpet single into A&M Records, the Whipped Cream album and a 1968 No. 1 with This Guy's in Love with You.
- [The Four Seasons: Frankie Valli, Sherry and Four No. 1s](https://1960smusic.net/blog/artists/the-four-seasons/): The Four Seasons formed in Newark in 1960 and reached No. 1 with Sherry, Big Girls Don't Cry, Walk Like a Man and Rag Doll between 1962 and 1964.
- [Patsy Cline: Crazy, the Nashville Sound and 1963](https://1960smusic.net/blog/artists/patsy-cline/): Patsy Cline went from Winchester, Virginia to Decca stardom with I Fall to Pieces and Crazy in 1961, then died in a plane crash on March 5, 1963, at 30.
- [The Temptations: Motown's Five-Man Detroit Soul Group](https://1960smusic.net/blog/artists/the-temptations/): The Temptations rose from Detroit to Motown stardom. Meet the five voices behind My Girl, the David Ruffin years, Norman Whitfield's psychedelic soul and Cloud Nine.
- [The Sonics: Tacoma's Screaming Garage Rock Pioneers](https://1960smusic.net/blog/artists/the-sonics/): The Sonics, a Tacoma garage band, cut The Witch and Psycho in 1964-65. Meet the lineup, the raw records and the proto-punk legacy they left behind.
- [Simon & Garfunkel: Folk-Rock Duo From Queens, New York](https://1960smusic.net/blog/artists/simon-and-garfunkel/): Simon & Garfunkel went from a flopped 1964 debut to three US No. 1s. Meet the Queens duo, the Sound of Silence overdub, The Graduate and the 1970 split.
- [The Jimi Hendrix Experience: Three Years That Rewired Rock](https://1960smusic.net/blog/artists/the-jimi-hendrix-experience/): The Jimi Hendrix Experience formed in London in 1966 and changed electric guitar in three albums. Meet the trio, the hits and the breakup.
- [Frank Sinatra: Reprise Records, Hits and My Way](https://1960smusic.net/blog/artists/frank-sinatra/): Frank Sinatra launched Reprise Records in 1960, then scored US No. 1 hits with Strangers in the Night and Somethin' Stupid before recording My Way in 1968.
- [Johnny Cash: From Ring of Fire to Folsom Prison](https://1960smusic.net/blog/artists/johnny-cash/): Johnny Cash went from Sun Records rockabilly to Columbia's biggest country star, with Ring of Fire in 1963 and the Folsom and San Quentin prison albums.
- [The Monkees: TV Band, Hit Singles and Headquarters](https://1960smusic.net/blog/artists/the-monkees/): The Monkees went from a 1966 NBC sitcom to three US No. 1 singles and four No. 1 albums, then fought for control and made Headquarters in 1967.
- [The Supremes: Motown's Hit Machine of the 1960s](https://1960smusic.net/blog/artists/the-supremes/): The Supremes went from the no-hit Detroit trio of 1961 to Motown's biggest act, with five straight US number ones. Their story, hits and lineup changes.
- [Bob Dylan: From Hibbing Folk Singer to Electric Poet](https://1960smusic.net/blog/artists/bob-dylan/): Bob Dylan went from Greenwich Village folk singer to the 1960s' most argued-over songwriter, plugging in at Newport and changing rock with Like a Rolling Stone.
- [The Beach Boys: California's Surf-Pop Pioneers](https://1960smusic.net/blog/artists/the-beach-boys/): The Beach Boys turned Hawthorne, California garage rehearsals into Pet Sounds and Good Vibrations, becoming 1960s surf pop's most influential and tragic band.
- [The Doors: Jim Morrison's Psychedelic Rock Legacy](https://1960smusic.net/blog/artists/the-doors/): The Doors fused Jim Morrison's poetry with Ray Manzarek's organ to become one of the defining, most controversial bands of 1960s psychedelic rock.
- [The Searchers Band: Merseybeat's Longest-Running Hitmakers](https://1960smusic.net/blog/artists/the-searchers/): The Searchers band rode jangling twelve-string guitars from Liverpool clubs to three UK number ones, becoming Merseybeat's longest-running touring act.
- [Herman's Hermits: The Band That Briefly Outsold the Beatles](https://1960smusic.net/blog/artists/hermans-hermits/): Herman's Hermits rode singalong hits and Peter Noone's boyish charm to the top of the 1965 US charts, briefly outselling the Beatles during the British Invasion.
- [The Dave Clark 5: Britain's Drum-Driven Answer to the Beatles](https://1960smusic.net/blog/artists/the-dave-clark-five/): The Dave Clark 5 knocked the Beatles off number one, played the Ed Sullivan Show a record 18 times, then vanished for decades when Dave Clark shelved the tapes.
- [The Animals: The Band That Found Jimi Hendrix](https://1960smusic.net/blog/artists/the-animals/): The Animals rode House of the Rising Sun to a transatlantic No. 1, then watched bassist Chas Chandler go on to discover Jimi Hendrix.
- [The Yardbirds: The Band That Launched Clapton, Beck and Page](https://1960smusic.net/blog/artists/the-yardbirds/): The Yardbirds turned a London R&B club act into the band that launched Eric Clapton, Jeff Beck and Jimmy Page before splitting into Led Zeppelin in 1968.
- [The Who: How a Smashed Guitar Became a Rock Signature](https://1960smusic.net/blog/artists/the-who/): The Who turned a broken guitar and an onstage explosion into rock history, then reinvented the album with Tommy and Who's Next.
- [The Kinks: How Getting Banned From America Changed Them](https://1960smusic.net/blog/artists/the-kinks/): How a slashed amp, a bloody onstage fight, and a four-year US touring ban turned Ray Davies into one of rock's most English songwriters.
- [Brian Jones Rolling Stones: The Founder Behind the Band](https://1960smusic.net/blog/artists/the-rolling-stones/): How a 20-year-old blues fanatic built the Rolling Stones, named it after Muddy Waters, and lost it before his death in 1969.
- [The Beatles: The Liverpool Band That Changed Music Forever](https://1960smusic.net/blog/artists/the-beatles/): How four teenagers from Liverpool became the most influential band in music history, from Hamburg's clubs to the studio innovations of Revolver and Sgt. Pepper.

## Songs
- [Sha La La La Lee: The Small Faces' 1966 UK Hit](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/sha-la-la-la-lee-small-faces/): Sha La La La Lee was the hit the Small Faces never wanted. How Don Arden, Kenny Lynch and Mort Shuman gave the mod band a UK No. 3 in March 1966.
- [White Rabbit by Jefferson Airplane: How Grace Slick Wrote It](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/white-rabbit-jefferson-airplane/): White Rabbit by Jefferson Airplane: Grace Slick wrote it on a $50 piano from Alice in Wonderland, and it hit No. 8 in 1967. The full story.
- [Somebody to Love: Jefferson Airplane's First Hit, 1967](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/somebody-to-love-jefferson-airplane/): Somebody to Love was Darby Slick's song for the Great Society before Jefferson Airplane took it to No. 5 in 1967. How the band's first hit was made.
- [This Guy's in Love with You: Herb Alpert's Vocal No. 1](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/this-guys-in-love-with-you-herb-alpert-and-the-tijuana-brass/): This Guy's in Love with You gave Herb Alpert his first No. 1 in 1968. The Bacharach and David song, the TV special, the one-take vocal and the covers.
- [Spanish Flea by Herb Alpert & The Tijuana Brass](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/spanish-flea-herb-alpert-and-the-tijuana-brass/): Spanish Flea by Herb Alpert & The Tijuana Brass: Julius Wechter's 1965 marimba-and-trumpet tune, a UK No. 3 hit and the sound of The Dating Game.
- [A Taste of Honey: Herb Alpert's Four-Grammy Hit](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/a-taste-of-honey-herb-alpert-and-the-tijuana-brass/): A Taste of Honey by Herb Alpert & The Tijuana Brass hit No. 7 in 1965. The Broadway origin, the Gold Star session, the kick drum that stayed and four Grammys.
- [Big Girls Don't Cry by The Four Seasons: A Movie Line](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/big-girls-dont-cry-four-seasons/): Big Girls Don't Cry gave The Four Seasons their second No. 1. See the disputed movie-line origin, the Chicago session and the five-week chart run.
- [Sherry by The Four Seasons: A 15-Minute No. 1](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/sherry-four-seasons/): Sherry by The Four Seasons went to No. 1 in 1962. See the 15-minute writing story, the disputed title origin, the two-take session and the five-week run.
- [Walk Like a Man by The Four Seasons: Smoke and a No. 1](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/walk-like-a-man-four-seasons/): Walk Like a Man was the Four Seasons' tougher third No. 1. See how Crewe and Gaudio wrote it, the smoky session story and the March 1963 chart run.
- [Crazy by Patsy Cline: The Willie Nelson Song She Made Hers](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/crazy-patsy-cline/): Crazy by Patsy Cline began as Willie Nelson's demo. See the Billy Walker trade, the one-take vocal on September 15, 1961, and how it hit No. 9.
- [I Fall to Pieces by Patsy Cline: Rejected Twice, Then No. 1](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/i-fall-to-pieces-patsy-cline/): I Fall to Pieces by Patsy Cline was turned down by Brenda Lee and Roy Drusky. See the November 1960 session, the radio fight and the No. 1 country run.
- [My Girl by The Temptations: The 1965 No. 1 Story](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/my-girl-temptations/): My Girl by The Temptations was the 1965 Smokey Robinson song that gave David Ruffin his big lead. Here is how it was made, charted and remembered.
- [Get Ready by The Temptations: The 1966 Kendricks Showcase](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/get-ready-temptations/): Get Ready by The Temptations was Smokey Robinson's last song for the group. See how it topped the R&B chart, then became a pop hit for Rare Earth.
- [The Sound of Silence: Simon & Garfunkel's 1965 Hit](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/the-sound-of-silence-simon-and-garfunkel/): The Sound of Silence flopped as an acoustic track, then hit No. 1 after a secret electric overdub. Read how Simon & Garfunkel's folk rock classic was made.
- [The Boxer by Simon & Garfunkel: Story of the 1969 Hit](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/the-boxer-simon-and-garfunkel/): The Boxer by Simon & Garfunkel grew from a placeholder chorus and a hotel Bible. Read how the 1969 hit was made, with a cannon-shot drum and 100 hours of work.
- [Scarborough Fair/Canticle by Simon & Garfunkel: Story](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/scarborough-fair-canticle-simon-and-garfunkel/): Scarborough Fair/Canticle by Simon & Garfunkel joins an old English ballad to an anti-war counter-melody. Read how it was made, who taught Paul Simon, and the credit row.
- [Hey Joe by The Jimi Hendrix Experience: 1966 Story](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/hey-joe-jimi-hendrix-experience/): Hey Joe by The Jimi Hendrix Experience was recorded in two hours on October 23, 1966. Here is who wrote it, who cut it first and how Hendrix made it his.
- [The Witch by The Sonics: 1964 Garage Rock Story](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/the-witch-sonics/): The Witch by The Sonics was cut in July 1964 in Seattle. Here is who wrote it, how a radio ban shaped its run and why it still sounds so wild.
- [Have Love, Will Travel by The Sonics: 1965 Garage Cover](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/have-love-will-travel-sonics/): Have Love, Will Travel by The Sonics took Richard Berry's 1959 R&B song and made it a garage-rock classic. Here is how the cover came together.
- [Strangers in the Night by Frank Sinatra: 1966 Story](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/strangers-in-the-night-frank-sinatra/): Strangers in the Night by Frank Sinatra began as a film instrumental called Beddy Bye. Here is how a rushed 1966 session made it a No. 1 hit Sinatra disliked.
- [My Way by Frank Sinatra: The 1968 Story Behind the Song](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/my-way-frank-sinatra/): My Way by Frank Sinatra began as a French pop song about a dying marriage. Here is how Paul Anka rewrote it overnight and Sinatra cut it in one take.
- [A World Without Love: Peter and Gordon's 1964 No. 1](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/a-world-without-love-peter-and-gordon/): A World Without Love was a Paul McCartney song the Beatles passed on. Here is how Peter and Gordon turned it into a 1964 number one in the UK and US.
- [Purple Haze by The Jimi Hendrix Experience: 1967 Story](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/purple-haze-jimi-hendrix-experience/): Purple Haze by The Jimi Hendrix Experience was written in December 1966 and recorded in January 1967. Here is how the riff, the fuzz and the legend came together.
- [Fly Me to the Moon by Frank Sinatra: 1964 Story](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/fly-me-to-the-moon-frank-sinatra/): Fly Me to the Moon by Frank Sinatra began as a 1954 waltz called In Other Words. Here is how Quincy Jones and Count Basie made it a swing standard that reached Apollo 10.
- [I'm a Believer: The Monkees' 1966 Hit by Neil Diamond](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/im-a-believer-monkees/): I'm a Believer was The Monkees' 1966 hit, written by Neil Diamond. Here is how it was recorded, why it topped the US and UK charts, and who has covered it since.
- [Last Train to Clarksville: The Monkees' 1966 No. 1 Hit](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/last-train-to-clarksville-monkees/): Last Train to Clarksville was The Monkees' debut single, written by Boyce and Hart. Here is how it was made, what it means, and how it hit number one in 1966.
- [Daydream Believer by The Monkees: 1967 No. 1 Story](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/daydream-believer-monkees/): Daydream Believer by The Monkees was written by John Stewart and spent four weeks at number one in 1967. Here is the story of its rejections, lyric change and recording.
- [Baby Love by The Supremes: The 1964 No. 1 Story](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/baby-love-supremes/): Baby Love by The Supremes was the 1964 Holland-Dozier-Holland follow-up to Where Did Our Love Go. Here is how it was made, charted and remembered.
- [Where Did Our Love Go: The Supremes' First No. 1 Story](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/where-did-our-love-go-supremes/): Where Did Our Love Go was the 1964 Holland-Dozier-Holland single that gave The Supremes their first No. 1. Here is how it was made and charted.
- [You Keep Me Hangin' On: The Supremes' 1966 No. 1 Story](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/you-keep-me-hangin-on-supremes/): You Keep Me Hangin' On was the 1966 Holland-Dozier-Holland rocker that gave The Supremes their eighth No. 1. Here is how it was made and charted.
- [Come See About Me: The Supremes' 1964 No. 1 Story](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/come-see-about-me-supremes/): Come See About Me was the 1964 Holland-Dozier-Holland hit that gave The Supremes their third straight No. 1. Here is how it was made and charted.
- [Ring of Fire: Johnny Cash's 1963 Country No. 1 Story](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/ring-of-fire-johnny-cash/): Ring of Fire was Johnny Cash's 1963 country No. 1, co-written by June Carter and Merle Kilgore. Here is the story of the mariachi horns, the charts and the authorship dispute.
- [Stop! In the Name of Love: The Supremes' 1965 No. 1](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/stop-in-the-name-of-love-supremes/): Stop! In the Name of Love is the 1965 Supremes hit by Holland-Dozier-Holland. Here is how it was written, recorded, staged and charted.
- [Subterranean Homesick Blues: Bob Dylan's 1965 Hit](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/subterranean-homesick-blues-bob-dylan/): Subterranean Homesick Blues was Bob Dylan's 1965 rapid-fire single. Here is the story, the session, the cue card clip and what the lyrics mean.
- [The Times They Are a-Changin': Dylan's 1964 Anthem](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/the-times-they-are-a-changin-bob-dylan/): The Times They Are a-Changin' is Bob Dylan's 1963 protest anthem. Here is how he wrote it, how it was recorded, what it means and who covered it.
- [Positively 4th Street by Bob Dylan: The 1965 Single](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/positively-4th-street-bob-dylan/): Positively 4th Street was Bob Dylan's bitter 1965 follow-up to Like a Rolling Stone. Here is the story, the session and who the song may be about.
- [Like a Rolling Stone by Bob Dylan: Story of the 1965 Hit](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/like-a-rolling-stone-bob-dylan/): Like a Rolling Stone grew from pages of verse into Bob Dylan's 1965 No. 2 hit. Here is the story of the session, the organ and the legacy.
- [Blowin' in the Wind by Bob Dylan: Story of the 1963 Song](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/blowin-in-the-wind-bob-dylan/): Blowin' in the Wind began as a two-verse Greenwich Village tune in 1962. Here is how Bob Dylan's song became an anthem for a generation.
- [California Girls by The Beach Boys: Story of the 1965 Hit](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/california-girls-beach-boys/): California Girls came to Brian Wilson during his first LSD trip and became The Beach Boys' 1965 No. 3 hit. Here is the full story.
- [Surfin' Safari by The Beach Boys: Story of the 1962 Hit](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/surfin-safari-beach-boys/): Surfin' Safari by The Beach Boys was the band's first Capitol single in 1962. Here is how it was written, recorded and charted.
- [Fun, Fun, Fun by The Beach Boys: Story Behind the 1964 Hit](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/fun-fun-fun-beach-boys/): Fun, Fun, Fun put a borrowed Chuck Berry guitar intro and a Thunderbird joyride into The Beach Boys' 1964 top five hit. Here is the full story.
- [Good Vibrations by The Beach Boys: Story Behind the 1966 Hit](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/good-vibrations-beach-boys/): Good Vibrations by The Beach Boys took seven months and four studios to build, mixing an Electro-Theremin into the pocket symphony that hit No. 1 in 1966.
- [Surfin USA by The Beach Boys: Story Behind the 1963 Hit](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/surfin-usa-beach-boys/): Surfin USA turned a borrowed Chuck Berry riff into The Beach Boys' first top five hit and the song that defined American surf rock in 1963.
- [The Crystal Ship: The Doors' 1967 Breakup Ballad](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/the-crystal-ship-doors/): The Crystal Ship is Jim Morrison's farewell to his first serious girlfriend, a piano led ballad The Doors tucked onto their 1967 debut album.
- [Album Strange Days: Inside The Doors' 1967 Moog Turn](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/strange-days-doors/): The album Strange Days pushed The Doors into darker, theatrical ground in 1967, with an early Moog vocal effect and a Sniffen Court street shoot for the cover.
- [The End by The Doors: Story Behind the 11-Minute Epic](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/the-end-doors/): The End by The Doors began as a breakup song, got the band fired from the Whisky a Go Go, and became the closing epic of Apocalypse Now.
- [The Doors Light My Fire: Story Behind Their Breakthrough Hit](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/light-my-fire-doors/): The Doors Light My Fire grew from Robby Krieger's first finished song into a number one hit that got the band banned from The Ed Sullivan Show.
- [Do Wah Diddy Diddy: The Story of Manfred Mann's No. 1 Hit](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/do-wah-diddy-diddy-manfred-mann/): Do Wah Diddy Diddy turned a flop by The Exciters into a transatlantic No. 1 for Manfred Mann in 1964, care of songwriters Jeff Barry and Ellie Greenwich.
- [Henry the 8th Herman's Hermits: The Song That Dethroned the Stones](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/im-henry-the-viii-i-am-hermans-hermits/): Henry the 8th Herman's Hermits turned a 1910 music hall song into a two-minute 1965 number one that knocked The Rolling Stones off the Billboard top spot.
- [Needles and Pins: How The Searchers Topped the UK Chart](https://1960smusic.net/blog/songs/needles-and-pins-searchers/): Needles and Pins turned a Jackie DeShannon flop into The Searchers' first UK number one, helped along by a studio accident and a squeaky bass drum pedal.
